system:
You are a senior methodologist designing candidate analysis plans for a biomedical data-analysis agent. You receive a compiled objective, a measured data profile with numbered difficulties, a catalogue of executable components, lessons from earlier projects, and resource limits. Design 1 complete, executable, genuinely different analysis plans.

The candidate pool is built over several calls so that each plan can be thought through properly. This is call 1 of 8 in this round; 0 plan(s) proposed earlier are listed at the end of the user message. Your plans must differ in design from all of them and widen the coverage of the three diversity directions.

What a plan is
A plan is a whole analysis design, not a model name: analysis unit, inputs and their representation, preprocessing, model, training, the plan's own validation design, metrics, and the conclusion it would be entitled to draw. Each plan will be executed exactly as you write it, so every field must be concrete.

Level of ambition
- Design at the level a methods paper would use, not at the level of a textbook exercise. This question is hard because many approaches are feasible and the complex ones can fail in ways a score does not show.
- Exactly ONE plan in this call must be the simplest valid plan (complexity "simple_reference"); it exists to show what the complex plans buy. Every other plan must be ambitious.
- Ambitious plans (complexity "ambitious") are deep, non-linear, joint latent-variable, gene- or patient-specific multi-component designs, or combinations of these, built mainly from the AMBITIOUS tier. Ridge, k-nearest-neighbour and partial-least-squares regressions are baselines and may not be the core of an ambitious plan.
- Complexity earns nothing by itself. Each ambitious plan must say which measured difficulty it addresses and why the added machinery should help with it.

Diversity
Spread the plans along three directions and use at least two clearly different values on each:
- data: which inputs and representations;
- model: model type and capacity;
- method: overall strategy (for example per-feature versus joint modelling, single model versus ensemble, how modalities are fused, how the validation is designed).
Do not submit two plans that differ only by a hyper-parameter or an encoder name.

Validity
- Respect allowed and forbidden inputs of the objective.
- Each plan chooses its own validation design from the options in the catalogue and reports its own score with it. Choose it deliberately; it will be judged.
- Every ambitious plan must be able to show a training curve and a convergence statement, and a direct comparison with the simple reference and the required comparators.
- Declare a budget. A full run of one plan must fit in 120 minutes on one job (32 CPU cores; a GPU may or may not be available, so say whether the plan needs one).

Components
Use component keys and parameter names exactly as in the catalogue. If an idea needs a component the catalogue lacks, you may propose it: put a new key in model.component and describe it in new_components (name, what it computes, inputs, outputs, training). Proposals are implemented only if feasible within the budget, so at most 1 plans may depend on a new component.

Be compact: summary at most 90 words, rationale at most 50 words, no padding in any field.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"plans": [ {
  "plan_id": any short label,
  "name": short name,
  "summary": 3-5 sentences in plain language describing the design and what it would let us conclude; no results, no predictions of scores,
  "complexity": "simple_reference" | "ambitious",
  "analysis_unit": string,
  "inputs": object following the catalogue's input representations,
  "preprocessing": [string],
  "model": {"component": key, "params": {...}},
  "fusion": string or null (only where the catalogue defines fusion),
  "training": {...},
  "validation": {...},
  "metrics": [string],
  "allowed_conclusions": string,
  "budget": {"needs_gpu": bool, "pilot_minutes": number, "full_minutes": number, "cpus": integer},
  "diversity": {"data": short label, "model": short label, "method": short label},
  "rationale": 2-4 sentences,
  "difficulties_addressed": [difficulty ids],
  "new_components": [ {"name": key, "description": string} ]
} ] }

COMPILED OBJECTIVE:
{
 "question": "Using the paired RNA and ATAC measurements, learn the cross-modal relationship. For cells of the same donor that took no part in training and for which only ATAC is provided, for which genes can the variation in RNA expression be predicted reliably?",
 "task_family": "cross_modal_prediction",
 "analysis_unit": "single cell (individual nucleus from the single healthy PBMC donor)",
 "estimand": "Per-gene Pearson correlation between ATAC-predicted and binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA across unseen donor cells, and per-gene correlation gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline.",
 "target": "Log-normalised RNA expression of frozen in-scope genes per unseen cell, scored against an independent binomial-thinned half of raw UMI counts.",
 "allowed_inputs": [
  "Paired RNA UMI counts and ATAC peak fragment counts of development cells",
  "ATAC peak fragment counts of held-out cells at prediction time only",
  "Peak-to-gene annotations with TSS distances and promoter/distal flags, plus gene start coordinates",
  "Frozen list of in-scope genes and frozen baseline cluster count from development cells",
  "Curated joint-modality development cell-type annotations solely for descriptive summaries and within-cluster diagnostics on development splits"
 ],
 "forbidden_inputs": [
  "Held-out cells' RNA counts (full or thinned halves) during training, tuning, or prediction",
  "Held-out cells' ATAC counts during model training, preprocessing, latent-space fitting, clustering, or hyperparameter selection",
  "Curated WNN cell-type annotations as model inputs for unseen cells or as evaluation ground truth",
  "Smoothed, imputed, denoised, or unthinned full-depth RNA expression as the validation scoring target",
  "Validation-split cells' RNA or ATAC during training, feature transformation, baseline clustering, or model selection",
  "External donor datasets, atlases, or pretrained model weights outside the provided paired Multiome measurements"
 ],
 "forbidden_reasons": {
  "Held-out cells' RNA counts (full or thinned halves) during training, tuning, or prediction": "Direct target leakage; the question asks to predict RNA expression when only ATAC is provided.",
  "Held-out cells' ATAC counts during model training, preprocessing, latent-space fitting, clustering, or hyperparameter selection": "Violates the requirement that target cells took no part in training, leaking test-set ATAC distributions.",
  "Curated WNN cell-type annotations as model inputs for unseen cells or as evaluation ground truth": "Derived jointly from RNA and ATAC; unavailable when only ATAC is provided and circular as evaluation truth.",
  "Smoothed, imputed, denoised, or unthinned full-depth RNA expression as the validation scoring target": "Overstates correlation above the measurement noise ceiling and mismatches the evaluator's unsmoothed binomial-thinned RNA target.",
  "Validation-split cells' RNA or ATAC during training, feature transformation, baseline clustering, or model selection": "Cross-split leakage biases out-of-sample correlation estimates, confidence intervals, and gene-level false discovery rate control.",
  "External donor datasets, atlases, or pretrained model weights outside the provided paired Multiome measurements": "Invalidates learning the cross-modal relationship strictly from the provided paired RNA and ATAC donor data."
 },
 "required_comparators": [
  "Floor 1 (cell-type baseline): ATAC-cluster mean RNA expression using the frozen development cluster count",
  "Floor 2 (gene activity): unlearned sum of ATAC counts over promoter and linked nearby peaks",
  "Floor 3 (sequencing depth): regression predicting log-normalised RNA from log ATAC sequencing depth alone",
  "Floor 4 (simple learners): ridge, k-nearest-neighbour, and partial-least-squares regression on the ATAC latent space",
  "Noise ceiling: RNA-to-RNA model fit on training cells predicting unseen cells' thinned half B from half A",
  "Permutation null: cell-permuted correlation distribution used to identify unjudgeable genes whose ceiling fails noise"
 ],
 "primary_metric": "Per-gene Pearson correlation r against binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA (half B) across unseen cells, evaluated via paired-bootstrap correlation gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline and mean per-gene r.",
 "secondary_metrics": [
  "Counts and identities of in-scope genes assigned to unjudgeable, not-beyond-cell-type, and reliably-predicted-beyond-cell-type decision groups",
  "Ratio of achieved per-gene Pearson correlation to the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling across judgeable in-scope genes",
  "Within-cluster Pearson correlation per gene alongside pooled correlation across development splits to assess rare cell populations",
  "Empirical coverage and width of paired-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for per-gene correlation estimates across validation folds"
 ],
 "acceptance_criteria": [
  {
   "id": "A1",
   "statement": "Training, selection, and prediction use no held-out RNA, no held-out ATAC in fitting, and no WNN labels.",
   "check": "no_forbidden_inputs",
   "rule": "Verify input lineage so every learned transformation, cluster, and weight uses only allowed development-cell inputs."
  },
  {
   "id": "A2",
   "statement": "Preprocessing, ATAC latent embeddings, baseline clustering, and model selection are strictly nested without evaluation cells.",
   "check": "selection_nested",
   "rule": "Fit scalers, embeddings, clusters, and hyperparameter choices inside inner training folds; compute reported scores on untouched outer-fold cells."
  },
  {
   "id": "A3",
   "statement": "Validation correlations are computed against unsmoothed, binomial-thinned half-count log-normalised RNA of unseen cells.",
   "check": "scored_on_unsmoothed_truth",
   "rule": "Split each unseen validation cell's raw UMI counts via independent binomial thinning into halves A and B; score against log-normalised half B."
  },
  {
   "id": "A4",
   "statement": "Candidate model, noise ceiling, permutation null, and all floor baselines are scored on identical unseen cells.",
   "check": "both_arms_same_units",
   "rule": "Compute Pearson r across the exact same outer-fold cells, identical thinned target half B, frozen in-scope genes, and identical zero-variance handling."
  },
  {
   "id": "A5",
   "statement": "Biological claims require beating technical depth and gene-activity floors; reliable-gene claims require beating the cell-type floor.",
   "check": "beats_required_floors",
   "rule": "Derive floor thresholds from comparator scores on identical validation cells: aggregate mean r must exceed depth and gene-activity floors; adopted learners must justify complexity against simple learners."
  },
  {
   "id": "A6",
   "statement": "Gene-level claims of reliable prediction beyond cell identity control false discoveries across all in-scope genes.",
   "check": "multiplicity_controlled",
   "rule": "Place genes whose ceiling fails the permutation null into unjudgeable; call remaining genes reliable only if paired-bootstrap r exceeds Floor 1 after Benjamini-Hochberg across all in-scope genes at 5% FDR."
  },
  {
   "id": "A7",
   "statement": "Each in-scope gene's correlation estimate and gain over the cell-type baseline include 95% confidence intervals.",
   "check": "interval_reported",
   "rule": "Compute two-sided 95% confidence intervals empirically from the paired-bootstrap distribution across unseen evaluation cells."
  },
  {
   "id": "A8",
   "statement": "Deliverable includes the finite held-out prediction matrix, reliable gene list, and per-gene correlation intervals.",
   "check": "deliverable_complete",
   "rule": "Confirm matrix shape equals held-out cells by frozen in-scope genes on the log-normalised scale with only finite values, plus complete gene lists and intervals."
  }
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "Unjudgeable due to measurement noise: for every in-scope gene, the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling fails to exceed the cell-permutation null.",
  "Confounded by sequencing depth: judgeable genes exist, but ATAC predictors fail to exceed the technical ATAC-depth baseline across unseen donor cells.",
  "No gene predicted beyond cell identity: predictors beat the depth baseline, but no judgeable in-scope gene significantly beats the ATAC cluster-mean baseline at 5% FDR.",
  "Specific genes predicted beyond cell identity: predictors beat technical floors, and an identified non-empty set of judgeable genes beats the ATAC cluster-mean baseline at 5% FDR."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Applies solely to unseen granulocyte-depleted PBMCs from this single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay; shows nothing about generalisation across other donors, tissues, disease states, granulocytes, or causal gene regulation.",
 "notes": "Partition every in-scope gene across the defined decision groups; report within-cluster alongside pooled correlations to expose rare-population underfitting; fit the final model on development cells alone before predicting held-out ATAC."
}

DATASET DESCRIPTION (from the data provider):
name: 10x Genomics Multiome, PBMC from one healthy donor (granulocytes removed, about 10k cells)
unit: cell
description: 'Each development cell has two count vectors measured in the same nucleus: RNA (UMI counts per gene)
  and ATAC (fragment counts per accessibility peak). Held-out cells of the same donor provide ATAC only. A peak
  annotation links each peak to nearby genes with the distance to the transcription start site and a promoter/distal
  flag. Gene start coordinates are available.'
label_provenance:
  statement: The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities
    jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement.
  implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it
    cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.
scope_of_inference: cells of the same donor that were not used for training; nothing about other donors
how_predictions_are_scored: 'The evaluator holds the RNA of the held-out cells. Each held-out cell''s RNA reads
  were split at random into two independent halves, A and B (binomial thinning). Every method is scored against
  half B after log-normalisation: for each gene, the Pearson correlation r between predicted and observed values
  across held-out cells. Genes in scope and the cluster number of the cell-type baseline were frozen from development
  cells only and are part of the view.'
rulers:
  ceiling: an RNA-to-RNA model that sees half A of the held-out cells and predicts half B; it marks what measurement
    noise allows
  floor_1_cell_type: cluster cells on ATAC, predict each cell by its cluster's mean expression (cluster number frozen
    from development cells)
  floor_2_gene_activity: sum of ATAC counts over the promoter and nearby peaks of the gene, no learning
  floor_3_depth: prediction from ATAC sequencing depth alone
  floor_4_simple_learners: ridge, k-nearest-neighbour and partial-least-squares regression on the ATAC latent space
decision_rule: '"Reliably predicted" means predicted beyond cell identity. Each in-scope gene is placed in one of
  three groups: (0) cannot be judged - the ceiling itself is not above the permutation null for this gene; (1) not
  beyond the cell-type baseline - the method''s r is not significantly above the cluster-mean baseline''s r; (2)
  predicts variation beyond cell type - the method''s r is significantly above the cluster-mean baseline''s r (paired
  bootstrap over cells, Benjamini-Hochberg across all in-scope genes, false discovery rate 5%). Thresholds come
  from the data by these rules; only the 5% false discovery rate and the 95% confidence level are conventions. An
  answer of "few or no genes are predicted beyond cell type" is acceptable if that is what the evidence shows.'
deliverable: A prediction matrix (held-out cells x in-scope genes, log-normalised scale), the list of genes the
  method claims to predict beyond cell type, and its own estimate of each gene's correlation with an interval.

MEASURED DATA PROFILE:
{
 "n_development_units": 7288,
 "n_held_out_units": 3124,
 "modalities": {
  "rna": {
   "features": 13536,
   "available_for": "development cells only",
   "fraction_zero": 0.8534380530643333,
   "median_counts_per_cell": 3830.0
  },
  "atac": {
   "features": 108377,
   "available_for": "all cells",
   "fraction_zero": 0.9281561742430454,
   "median_counts_per_cell": 20586.5
  }
 },
 "pairing": "both modalities measured in the same cell for every development cell",
 "genes_in_scope": 11282,
 "peak_gene_links": 87029,
 "cell_type_baseline_k": 20
}

MEASURED DIFFICULTIES (most severe first):
- D1 [measurement_noise, severity high] RNA counts are 85.3% zeros (median 3800 UMIs per cell). Splitting each cell's reads into two independent halves, a gene's value in one half correlates with the other half at a median r of 0.111 across 11282 in-scope genes (90th percentile 0.306). Implication: Per-gene correlation with a single noisy reading is bounded well below 1; scores must be read against a noise ceiling, and validating against smoothed or full-depth targets overstates accuracy.
- D2 [class_imbalance, severity high] The provided annotation has 19 cell types in the development set, from 1936 cells (CD14 Mono) down to 15 (Plasma). Implication: Rare populations contribute little to a pooled correlation and are easy to underfit; within-cluster correlation should be reported alongside the pooled one.
- D3 [multiple_comparisons, severity high] 11282 genes are in scope and each gets its own test. Implication: Gene-level claims need false-discovery-rate control across all in-scope genes.
- D4 [label_provenance, severity high] The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement. Implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.
- D5 [technical_confounding, severity medium] ATAC depth and RNA depth are correlated across cells (r = 0.36 on the log scale). A model that sees only ATAC depth reaches a mean per-gene r of 0.032. Implication: Report a depth-only baseline; a predictor must beat it before its signal is called biological.
- D6 [strong_baseline, severity medium] Predicting each cell by the mean expression of its ATAC cluster (k = 20, chosen by cross-validation inside the development set) gives a mean per-gene r of 0.130; ridge regression on the ATAC latent space gives 0.143; the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling is 0.194. Implication: Most predictable variation is cell identity. A plan answers the question only through what it predicts beyond the cluster-mean baseline, gene by gene, on the same cells.
- D7 [statistical_power, severity low] With thousands of cells a correlation as small as 0.037 already exceeds 95% of the permutation null (3124 held-out cells will be scored). Implication: Significance against zero is nearly automatic and cannot be the headline; effect size and the comparison with the cell-type baseline carry the conclusion.

COMPONENT CATALOGUE:
TASK FAMILY: cross_modal_prediction - Predict one measured modality from another, feature by feature, for units that provide only the source modality.

INPUT REPRESENTATIONS (field inputs):
  - lsi: TF-IDF on binarised peaks then truncated SVD; first (depth) component dropped. Compact global cell state. Parameters: n_components 20-150; max_peaks 20000-108377.
  - tfidf_peaks: Sparse TF-IDF over the most accessible peaks; high-dimensional input for a neural encoder. Parameters: max_peaks 10000-60000.
  - gene_activity: Per-gene sum of ATAC counts over annotated peaks, depth-normalised. One feature per in-scope gene. Parameters: mode promoter | promoter_and_distal.
  - cis_peaks: For each gene, the individual peaks within the window around its start site (gene-specific inputs). Parameters: window_kb 50-500; max_peaks_per_gene 5-50.
  - depth: Log ATAC depth of the cell as a covariate. Parameters: -.

BASIC TIER (baselines, the single simple reference, preprocessing):
  - cluster_mean: Cluster cells on LSI, predict each cell by its cluster's mean expression. This is ruler floor 1. Parameters: k: 'frozen' (the frozen cell-type baseline) or an integer. Cost: seconds, CPU.
  - latent_ridge: Ridge regression from LSI components to all genes. Parameters: alpha. Cost: seconds, CPU.
  - latent_knn: k-nearest-neighbour regression in LSI space. Parameters: k. Cost: seconds, CPU.
  - latent_pls: Partial least squares from LSI to all genes. Parameters: n_components. Cost: seconds, CPU.
  - gene_activity_score: Use the gene activity score itself as the prediction (no learning). Ruler floor 2. Parameters: mode. Cost: seconds, CPU.

AMBITIOUS TIER (what candidate plans are mainly built from):
  - residual_over_cluster_mean: Start from the cluster-mean prediction and train a non-linear model on what is left: the deviation of each cell from its cluster mean. Aims directly at variation beyond cell type. Parameters: learner mlp | gbm; hidden [..]; dropout; cluster_k 'frozen' | int. Cost: mlp: minutes on CPU; gbm: one boosted model per gene, tens of minutes on 32 CPUs.
  - cis_regulatory: Gene-specific model: each gene is predicted from the peaks near it plus a shared global cell state. masked_nn trains all genes jointly with a sparse peak-to-gene layer; gbm / elastic_net fit one model per gene. Parameters: learner masked_nn | gbm | elastic_net; window_kb; max_peaks_per_gene; global_state_dim; hidden. Cost: masked_nn: minutes on CPU; gbm: tens of minutes on 32 CPUs.
  - translation_network: Encoder-decoder network from the ATAC profile to all genes at once, trained with a count likelihood on raw UMI counts (library size as offset) or MSE on log-normalised values. Parameters: encoder_hidden [..]; latent_dim; decoder linear | mlp; likelihood poisson | nb | mse; dropout. Cost: 5-20 minutes on CPU, faster on GPU.
  - joint_latent_multivi: MultiVI joint variational model of both modalities, trained to convergence with early stopping on held-out reconstruction; expression of ATAC-only cells is imputed from the joint latent space. Parameters: n_latent; n_hidden; max_epochs; early_stopping_patience; n_peaks. Cost: 30-100 minutes; GPU preferred, CPU possible with a peak subset.
  - peakvi_latent_head: PeakVI latent representation of accessibility followed by a supervised prediction head. Parameters: n_latent; head mlp | ridge. Cost: 20-60 minutes.
  - contrastive_pretrain_head: First align the two modalities on development cells with a contrastive (CLIP-style) objective, then predict expression from the aligned ATAC embedding with a head, or by transferring expression from nearest RNA neighbours. Parameters: embed_dim; temperature; pretrain_epochs; head mlp | knn_transfer. Cost: 10-30 minutes on CPU.
  - multitask_lowrank: Joint prediction of all genes through a low-rank bottleneck with learned gene embeddings, so genes share statistical strength. Parameters: rank; trunk_hidden [..]; gene_embedding_dim. Cost: minutes on CPU.
  - stacking_ensemble: Combine heterogeneous models with out-of-fold predictions: a meta-learner weighs the members gene by gene. Members are refitted on all training cells. Parameters: members [list of {component, params, inputs}]; meta per_gene_ridge | global_weights; oof_folds 3-5. Cost: (oof_folds + 1) x the summed cost of the members.

TRAINING OPTIONS (field training): max_epochs; early_stopping_patience (epochs without improvement on an internal validation split); lr; batch_size; weight_decay; target_denoising none | knn_pool (k) - train against RNA pooled over the k nearest training cells (training cells only; scoring always uses unsmoothed values unless the validation design says otherwise)

VALIDATION DESIGN OPTIONS (field validation): scheme holdout | kfold; holdout_fraction 0.1-0.3; k 3-5; split_unit cell; scoring_target thinned_half (score against an independent half of each validation cell's reads, as the evaluator does) | full_depth (score against the unsplit log-normalised counts) | knn_smoothed (score against neighbour-pooled expression); n_seeds 1-3; compare_with [rulers to compute in the same split]; gene_claim_rule: how the plan decides which genes it claims are predicted beyond cell type

LESSONS FROM EARLIER PROJECTS (retrieved by difficulty):
- K4 (Project 3): MultiVI was trained for 50 epochs without early stopping and with logging disabled, so convergence could not be audited afterwards. Practice: Train latent-variable models with early stopping on held-out reconstruction and keep the loss history.
- K5 (Project 3): The objective required the joint representation to preserve structure at least as well as the best single modality; the selected model had a clustering ARI of 0.528 against 0.613 for RNA alone, and nobody checked. Practice: Turn every requirement in the objective into an explicit check that runs before a result is reported.
- K6 (Project 3): Fusion that included ER/PR/HER2 scored macro-F1 0.723, image only 0.645, and fusion without receptors 0.583. Which number answers the question depends on whether receptors are part of the question. Practice: Decide allowed and forbidden inputs from the question, and compare the arms the question names.
- K8 (Project 3): A baseline labelled as an ATAC decoder actually returned RNA principal components, and a re-implemented method overlapped the reference implementation at only 0.195. Practice: Check each baseline does what its name says on a case with a known answer before using it as a comparator.
- K1 (Project 1, first version): Two runs with identical inputs selected different methods because the deciding margin was smaller than run-to-run variation (a sub-second runtime difference broke the tie). Practice: Before ranking, measure the spread of the selection signal across seeds or resamples; treat differences inside that spread as ties.
- K10 (Projects 1-3): Planning was a rule-based filter over methods; alternatives were never compared as whole analysis designs, and the reports listed numbers without a conclusion. Practice: Compare complete plans (inputs, model, validation, permitted conclusion) and end with a stated conclusion and its limits.
- K3 (Project 2, first version): Four generative models were trained for about one minute in total; their samples were noise, and the negative conclusion followed from the tiny budget, not from the data. Practice: A complex model needs a training curve and a convergence statement before its score is read; an unconverged model is evidence about the budget only.
- K7 (Project 3): A fusion head trained with unweighted cross-entropy recalled 0 of 10 patients of the smallest class while its macro score still looked acceptable. Practice: Weight classes, use a class-balanced metric, and report recall for every class.

PLANS ALREADY PROPOSED: none yet.

plans.name: Nested LSI Multi-Output Ridge Reference
plans.summary: Each cell's ATAC profile is projected into a depth-filtered Latent Semantic Indexing space fitted strictly on training cells, and ridge regression predicts expression across all 11,282 target genes. Using nested five-fold cross-validation over three seeds, predictions on unseen cells are scored against binomial-thinned RNA alongside technical floors, the ATAC cluster-mean baseline, and an RNA noise ceiling. Paired bootstraps with false-discovery control identify which judgeable genes exceed cell identity. This simple reference quantifies what global linear chromatin state achieves alone.
preprocessing: Binarise ATAC peak fragment counts, fit TF-IDF inverse-document-frequency weights across all 108,377 peaks, and fit 51-component truncated SVD strictly on outer/inner training-fold development cells; drop component 1 (sequencing-depth axis) to retain 50 L2-normalised LSI features, projecting unseen validation and held-out cells out-of-sample without refitting.

Normalise training-fold raw RNA UMI counts per cell via log1p(1e4 * UMI / total_cell_UMI) using total UMI summed across all 13,536 measured genes, then slice target columns to the frozen 11,282 in-scope genes.

For unseen validation cells only, split raw RNA UMI counts via independent Binomial(UMI, 0.5) thinning into half A (solely for the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling input) and half B, computing unsmoothed log1p(1e4 * half_B / total_half_B_UMI) on the frozen 11,282 genes as the evaluation target.

Exclude held-out cells' ATAC and curated WNN labels from all fitting, clustering, and tuning steps, verify comparator sanity on synthetic known-answer checks, and set Pearson r = 0.0 identically across all arms whenever predicted or observed variance is zero.

validation.comparator_details: Fit k='frozen' (k=20) cluster_mean, promoter_and_distal gene_activity_score, log-ATAC-depth OLS, latent_knn, latent_pls, and RNA-to-RNA ridge ceiling (half A to half B) strictly inside each outer training fold; evaluate all arms on identical out-of-fold cells and identical thinned half B targets.
validation.gene_claim_rule: Assign in-scope genes whose RNA-to-RNA ceiling fails to beat the 1,000-shuffle cell-permutation null (one-sided p >= 0.05) to group 0 (unjudgeable); for remaining judgeable genes, compute 1,000 paired cell-bootstrap resamples of delta_r = r_model - r_floor1, apply Benjamini-Hochberg across all 11,282 in-scope genes at 5% FDR, and call genes with BH q < 0.05 and delta_r > 0 group 2 (reliably predicted beyond cell type), otherwise group 1 (not beyond cell type), auditing seed-to-seed stability.

metrics: Per-gene and mean Pearson correlation r against unsmoothed binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA (half B) across unseen out-of-fold cells
Per-gene paired-bootstrap correlation gain (delta_r = r_model - r_floor1) and empirical two-sided 95% confidence intervals for both r_model and delta_r
Gene counts and identities partitioned into (0) unjudgeable, (1) not-beyond-cell-type, and (2) reliably-predicted-beyond-cell-type at 5% BH-FDR across 11,282 genes
Ratio of achieved correlation to the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling (r_model / r_ceiling) across judgeable in-scope genes
Within-cluster per-gene Pearson r across frozen ATAC clusters and descriptive development WNN cell types (including rare Plasma cells) alongside pooled r
Empirical 95% CI coverage/width across folds, 3-seed selection spread, and automated A1-A8 verification of finite 3,124 x 11,282 held-out predictions
plans.allowed_conclusions: Select strictly one of the four objective-defined conclusions supported by nested validation (unjudgeable due to noise, confounded by depth, no gene beyond cell identity, or a specific 5%-FDR gene set predicted beyond cell identity by linear global chromatin state), scoped exclusively to unseen granulocyte-depleted PBMCs of this single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay with no cross-donor, granulocyte, causal, or non-linear optimality claims.
plans.rationale: Closed-form ridge regression on depth-filtered LSI establishes how much continuous RNA variation beyond discrete ATAC clusters is already linearly encoded in global chromatin state. Nested cross-validation against binomial-thinned counts provides a fast, leak-free yardstick that every ambitious model must justify exceeding.
